Zachary Macaulay
zak'ə-rē mə-kaw'lē
n. (Zachary Macaulay, 1768–1838, Clapham abolitionist, governor of Sierra Leone, editor of the Christian Observer)
Hebrew Zekaryah, the LORD has remembered; Gaelic MacAmhlaidh, son of Olaf.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Zachary Macaulay went out at sixteen as a bookkeeper and then manager on a Jamaica sugar estate, and what he administered there turned him for life. He came home, joined the Clapham circle, served as governor of Sierra Leone from 1794, and was captured by the French in the course of it; he then edited the Christian Observer for fourteen years and became the movement's statistician. His particular gift was the mastery of detail: he compiled and verified the returns, the shipping records, and the colonial registries, and it was Macaulay the committees sent for when a planter's figures needed testing. He worked on the registration of slaves as the means of exposing the illegal trade after 1807. He was the father of the historian Thomas Babington Macaulay. Job 31:15 is the question he carried out of Jamaica, “Did not he that made me in the womb make him?” (Job 31:15).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a registry as a book in which a record is kept, and an overseer as one who superintends others.

expand to see more

REG'ISTRY, n. The act of recording or writing in a register; the book or record in which entries are made.

OVERSEE'R, n. One who overlooks; a superintendent; an officer who has the care of the poor.

ESTATE', n. The interest or quantity of interest a man has in lands; property; fortune; a plantation.

Modern Corruption

He managed a sugar estate at twenty and spent the next forty years dismantling the system he had run.

expand to see more

Macaulay is the Clapham figure whose conversion to the cause was not theoretical. He had kept the books and given the orders, and he knew precisely which of the planters' published assurances were false and how to prove it. Job 31:15 is the text that undoes the whole apparatus of justification at a stroke, since a common Maker in the womb leaves no room for a difference of kind between the overseer and the overseen.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the sanctified use of tedium. Macaulay's contribution was columns of verified figures, maintained for decades, and without them the parliamentary speeches would have been sentiment. Exo 21:16 supplied the law and Pro 31:8 the duty; the registries supplied the proof that the law was being broken on a scale the trade's defenders denied. Isa 58:6 is what the figures were for.

Usage

"“Did not he that made me in the womb make him?” (Job 31:15) — what he brought back from Jamaica."

"“he that stealeth a man, and selleth him” (Exo 21:16) — the law his registries proved broken."

"“Open thy mouth for the dumb” (Pro 31:8) — in his case, in columns of figures."
